posts.title: Citation by publication, 146th District Court, Bell County: Cause No. 25DCV352411
posts.body:
Court: 146th Judicial District Court, Bell County, Texas (Bell County District Courts Building, Belton).
Cause No.: 25DCV352411. Suit by a mortgage lender to rescind a vendor's lien and assert superior title to residential property in Temple, Texas.
Petition filed: March 14, 2025. Citation issued: September 11, 2026.
Answer due: by 10:00 AM on the first Monday after 42 days from issuance, which by our count is Monday, October 26, 2026. Confirm the date with the Bell County District Clerk; a default judgment may be taken against a defendant who does not answer.
Published in the Killeen Daily Herald on October 1, 8, 15 and 22, 2026.
Defendant names and the property address are in the published notice linked below and in the court file; they are not repeated here.
posts.source_label: Witnessed by Scott Weeden (Killeen Daily Herald legal notices)

posts.title: Citation by publication, 169th District Court, Bell County: Cause No. 26DCV360297
posts.body:
Court: 169th Judicial District Court, Bell County, Texas (Bell County District Courts Building, Belton).
Cause No.: 26DCV360297. Suit by a federal mortgage agency, as trustee, concerning title to residential property in Killeen, Texas, including claims against the unknown heirs of a deceased borrower.
Petition filed: March 12, 2026. Citation issued: October 2, 2026.
Answer due: by 10:00 AM on the first Monday after 42 days from issuance, which by our count is Monday, November 16, 2026. Confirm the date with the Bell County District Clerk; a default judgment may be taken against a defendant who does not answer.
Published in the Killeen Daily Herald on October 8, 15, 22 and 29, 2026.
Defendant names and the property address are in the published notice linked below and in the court file; they are not repeated here.

posts.title: HUD notice of default and foreclosure sale, Temple property: sale November 3, 2026
posts.body:
Issuer: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, through its designated foreclosure commissioner (Single Family Mortgage Foreclosure Act of 1994, 12 U.S.C. 3751 et seq.). TS No. LO-54089-TX.
Nonjudicial foreclosure of a HUD-held deed of trust on residential property in Temple, Texas (Bell County).
Sale: Tuesday, November 3, 2026, between 10:00 AM and 1:00 PM, at public auction at the Bell County Clerk's alcove, Bell County Justice Complex, 1201 Huey Drive, Belton, Texas (or the area designated by the Commissioners Court).
Reinstatement: the notice states the amount required to reinstate before the sale, as of November 2, 2026. Bidders other than HUD must bring a 10% deposit by certified or cashier's check.
Published in the Killeen Daily Herald on October 1, 8 and 15, 2026.
Borrower names and the property address are in the published notice linked below; they are not repeated here.

posts.title: Representation opportunity: defendants in two Bell County title and lien suits (25DCV352411, 26DCV360297)
posts.body:
Defendants served by publication in two Bell County district court suits brought by mortgage lenders may need counsel before their answer deadlines: Cause No. 25DCV352411 (146th District Court, answer due by our count October 26, 2026) and Cause No. 26DCV360297 (169th District Court, answer due by our count November 16, 2026). Both concern title to residential property in Temple and Killeen; one includes the unknown heirs of a deceased borrower.
Legal Luminary does not represent these defendants and does not make offers or agree to fee terms on their behalf. Party information is in the public notices and the court files. Attorneys interested in defense, heirship, or title work in Bell County can review the files with the Bell County District Clerk and contact the parties directly, consistent with the Texas Disciplinary Rules of Professional Conduct.
A printable contingency fee agreement template is linked below. A defendant may choose to use it with an attorney willing to take the matter on contingency; it binds no one unless both the defendant and the attorney complete and sign it.
If you are a defendant in one of these cases, consider contacting a lawyer before the deadline. Lone Star Legal Aid and TexasLawHelp.org can help you find free or low-cost help.
posts.source_label: Witnessed by Scott Weeden (Killeen Daily Herald legal notices)
